extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of mathematics; general mathematical problem-solvers
extracted.subtask_description: Heuristic checklist for solving mathematical problems: understand the problem, devise a plan linking data to the unknown (including using auxiliary or related problems), carry out and check each step, and reflect on the solution. Intended for learners and instructors to guide problem-solving practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the problem
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the unknown? What are the data? What is the condition? Is it possible to satisfy the condition? Is the condition sufficient to determine the unknown? Or is it insufficient? Or redundant? Or contradictory?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draw a figure. Introduce suitable notation. Separate the various parts of the condition. Can you write them down? (These are prompting questions to ensure full comprehension of the problem statement and its constraints.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the connection between the data and the unknown / devise a plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Find the connection between the data and the unknown. You may be obliged to consider auxiliary problems if an immediate connection cannot be found. You should obtain eventually a plan of the solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look at the unknown and try to think of a familiar problem having the same or a similar unknown. Ask whether you can use a previously solved related problem, its result, or its method; whether you should introduce auxiliary elements to make such use possible; or whether you can restate the problem or return to definitions to reveal a route to a plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you seen it before / use related problems or theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you seen it before? Or have you seen the same problem in a slightly different form? Do you know a related problem? Do you know a theorem that could be useful?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a known result, method, or solved related problem can be applied directly or after suitable restatement/auxiliary construction. Explicitly ask: Could you use its result? Could you use its method? Should you introduce some auxiliary element in order to make its use possible?

rubrics_metrics.name: Try solving related or simpler/stronger versions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you cannot solve the proposed problem try to solve first some related problem. Could you imagine a more accessible related problem? A more general problem? A more special problem? An analogous problem? Could you solve a part of the problem?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep only a part of the condition and drop the other part; analyze how far the unknown is then determined and how it can vary. Solving related instances can suggest methods or partial results useful for the original problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change the unknown or the data to simplify
rubrics_metrics.description: Could you change the unknown or the data, or both if necessary, so that the new unknown and the new data are nearer to each other?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reformulate variables/unknowns or introduce new ones to make relationships clearer; consider substitutions or redefining the problem to bring data and unknown into closer form for existing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use all given information / account for essential notions
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you use all the data? Did you use the whole condition? Have you taken into account all essential notions involved in the problem?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly check whether any part of the statement has been ignored or whether some definitions/assumptions were overlooked; omission of data often leads to incorrect or incomplete solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw a figure and introduce suitable notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw a figure. Introduce suitable notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual representation and clear notation can reveal hidden structure, separate parts of the condition, and make planning and carrying out the solution easier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry out the plan and check each step
rubrics_metrics.description: Carry out your plan. Can you see clearly that the step is correct? Can you prove that it is correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When executing the plan, verify at each step that the logical deduction is valid and justified; write or supply proofs for assertions made in the solution rather than relying on intuition alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the solution obtained / verify the result
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the solution obtained. Can you check the result? Can you check the argument?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recompute, substitute back, or test special cases to verify correctness. Ensure no step depends on unstated assumptions or leaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Looking back: reflect, find alternative proofs, and generalize or apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you derive the result differently? Can you see it at a glance? Can you use the result, or the method, for some other problem?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek alternative proofs for insight and elegance, attempt to find a short or visual argument, and consider how the method or result can be generalized or applied elsewhere to deepen understanding and build problem-solving repertoire.
